title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates used by teams. It provides principles, owner responsibilities, and step-by-step procedures for common workflows.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with company systems, data, procurement, or travel booking processes. Exceptions must be approved by the owning team and recorded in the Related Pages section.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required for a role or task.
- Auditability: all elevated access, procurement, and material changes must be traceable with an owner, justification, and approval.
- Separation of duties: requestors, approvers, and implementers should be distinct when practical.
- Risk-based controls: apply stronger controls to higher-classified data or critical systems.

Owners and Escalation
--------------------
- Access & Permissions: Eng-SRE (owner: Claire Huang)
- Change Management: Eng-Platform (owner: Jonah Reed)
- Data Management: Security & Compliance (owner: Miguel Santos)
- Procurement & Expenses: Finance (owner: Priya Kaur)
- Vendor Management: Legal & Finance (owner: Samir Das)
- Travel: People Ops (owner: Aisha Patel)
General escalation: contact team owner; if unresolved within 48 hours, escalate to CTO/COO depending on domain.

1) Access & Permissions
-----------------------
Purpose: Standardize how access is requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, and revoked.

Access classifications:
- Level 0 (Public/internal): Company-wide docs with no PII or sensitive IP.
- Level 1 (Restricted): Internal systems (non-production) and low-sensitivity data.
- Level 2 (Sensitive): Production systems, customer data, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics. Requires justification and manager + security approval.
- Level 3 (Privileged): Admin/root-level access, ability to change infra, or production secrets. Requires business owner, security, and People Ops approval.

Request process (standard):
1. Submit request using the Access Request template (Internal Templates section). Include justification, duration, and expected scope.
2. Manager review: manager confirms business need within 3 business days.
3. Security review: for Level 2/3 within 2 business days.
4. Provisioning: Eng-SRE or IT performs provisioning and records changes in the provisioning log.
5. Post-provision review: owner verifies access is correct within 5 business days.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Use the Emergency Access form and notify the on-call SRE and Security; approvals retroactively required within 24 hours. Emergency sessions must be recorded and audited.

Periodic review:
- Quarterly review for Level 2/3 accounts; annual review for Level 1. Owners must attest to continued need. Non-attested access will be revoked after 30 days.

Access revocation:
- Offboarding: People Ops provides the offboarding list daily; IT/Eng-SRE must revoke access within 8 business hours for ex-employees.

Approval matrix (high-level):
| Access level | Requestor approval | Manager approval | Security approval | People Ops approval |
|-------------|-------------------|------------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| Level 0     | Self              | N/A              | N/A               | N/A                 |
| Level 1     | Self              | Manager          | N/A               | N/A                 |
| Level 2     | Manager           | Manager          | Security          | N/A                 |
| Level 3     | Manager           | Business owner   | Security          | People Ops          |

2) Change Management
---------------------
Purpose: Ensure changes to production systems are planned, tested, and reversible.

Change types:
- Standard (low-risk, pre-authorized): configuration updates that meet predefined checklists.
- Normal (planned): changes requiring CAB approval with scheduled windows.
- Emergency: fixes addressing incidents; follow emergency change process and postmortem.

Process for Normal changes:
1. Create a Change Request (use Change Request template) with description, rollback plan, test plan, impact analysis, and owner.
2. Submit to Change Board (CAB) at least 72 hours before proposed window.
3. CAB review: technical, security, and product stakeholders review risks and tests.
4. Approve and schedule: window assigned and communicated to on-call.
5. Execute: follow runbook; capture logs and deployment artifacts.
6. Verify and close: owner verifies success and updates the change log.

Emergency changes:
- Notify CAB and on-call immediately; implement with senior engineer and security present. Record actions and produce an incident-linked post-change review within 5 business days.

Rollback criteria:
- Explicit rollback criteria must be defined in every change request (e.g., error rate >1%, latency >200ms above baseline, or data loss observed).

Change windows and blackouts:
- Major releases: Saturdays 03:00–07:00 UTC preferred; product teams may require exceptions.
- No major infra changes during end-of-quarter financial close (finance to publish blackout dates annually).

3) Data Management
------------------
Classification and handling:
- Public/Internal: may be shared widely.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, contract terms, model weights not approved for public release.
- Restricted: regulated data (e.g., financial, health) requiring contractual and technical controls.

Data access requests:
- Use Data Access Request template; include business justification, retention needs, and receiving systems. Security will determine additional controls (DLP, VPC restrictions, encryption).

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: 7 years for financial records, 2 years for operational logs, 90 days for debug logs, unless otherwise required by contract or regulation.
- Data deletion requests: follow the Data Deletion Procedure (steps recorded in the request ticket).

Backups and restore:
- Critical datasets: daily backups with 30-day retention in immutable storage.
- Restore drills: quarterly restore drills for critical datasets; results published on the platform runbooks page.

Encryption and key management:
- All production sensitive data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using company-managed KMS. Key lifecycle managed per Security & Compliance guidelines.

Data breach response:
- Follow the Incident Response - Security playbook (link in Related Pages). Notify Legal and Customer Success within 24 hours of confirmed breach involving customer data.

4) Procurement & Expenses
------------------------
Procurement thresholds and roles:
- < $2,500: Individual contributor may purchase with manager approval (use company card or submit expense).
- $2,500–$25,000: Requires department head and Finance approval; Procurement team creates PO.
- > $25,000: Requires Procurement, Finance, and Legal review; contract required.

Procurement process:
1. Submit Procurement Request template with business case, preferred vendor, and budget code.
2. Procurement team validates vendor and pricing; Finance approves budget.
3. Purchase Order (PO) issued for approved requests.
4. Receipt and invoice: Finance matches invoice to PO; pay per vendor terms.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit Expense Report template with itemized receipts within 30 days.
- Credit card reconciliations must be completed monthly by cardholder; delinquent reconciliations may result in card suspension.

Travel booking and approvals (summary):
- Book via approved vendor partners or company travel portal.
- Domestic travel: manager approval. International travel: manager + People Ops approval.
- Travel over $5,000 requires Finance pre-approval.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Security questionnaire completed and risk scored.
- Contract reviewed by Legal (NDA and terms).
- Finance setup for payments and PO requirements.
- Data access scope documented; technical onboarding list provided.
- Approved only after Procurement, Legal, and Security sign-off.

Periodic review and renewals:
- Strategic vendors: annual review with Vendor Scorecard (security, performance, cost).
- Non-strategic vendors: review every 2 years.
- Contract renewals: commence negotiation 90 days before expiry.

Termination and exit plans:
- Ensure contract includes data return or secure deletion clauses. Maintain a documented exit procedure with technical contacts and timelines.

6) Travel Policies (details)
---------------------------
Booking rules:
- Use company preferred carriers when available. Economy for flights under 6 hours; business class requires People Ops + Exec approval for flights over 6 hours.
- Hotels: mid-tier business hotels near meeting location; avoid extended-stay properties unless approved.

Per diem & reimbursable items:
- Meals: up to $75/day in major metro areas, $50/day in smaller markets unless actuals are justified.
- Ground transport: rideshare or standard car rental; use receipts.
- Non-reimbursable: in-room movies, personal leisure charges, fines.

Safety and travel security:
- Register international travel with People Ops; follow travel advisories and country-specific requirements.
- Emergency contact: People Ops on-call (24/7) for travel incidents.

7) Internal Templates and Links
------------------------------
Canonical templates (use these for requests to ensure traceability):
- Access Request template (access-request-form)
- Change Request template (change-request-form)
- Data Access Request template (data-access-request-form)
- Procurement Request template (procurement-request-form)
- Expense Report template (expense-report-form)
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (vendor-onboarding-checklist)
- Travel Authorization form (travel-authorization-form)

Each template includes required fields, approvers, and instructions. Templates are stored in the company template library (Confluence templates and Google Drive links).

Operational Routines and Auditability
-----------------------------------
- Weekly: Procurement sends open PO report to Finance and requestors.
- Monthly: Access attestation reminders to owners for Level 2/3.
- Quarterly: CAB summary and change metrics published to the eng-platform dashboard.
- Annual: Vendor risk assessment and policy review cycle.

Non-Compliance and Exceptions
----------------------------
- Violations may result in temporary suspension of access, retraining, or disciplinary action depending on severity.
- Exception requests: submit Exception Request template with mitigation plans. Security & Legal must sign off for data or vendor-related exceptions.
